chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from Yunus ibn Abdul Rahman, from Dawud ibn Zurbiyy, who said:

I fell ill in Medina with a severe illness, and that reached Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So he wrote to me: 'It has reached me your illness. Buy one Sa'a of wheat, then lie on your back and scatter it upon your chest however it scatters, and say: O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which, when the distressed asks You by it, You remove the adversity from him, and establish him in the earth, and make him Your vicegerent upon Your creatures, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the People of his Household, and to cure me from my illness.' Then sit upright, gather the wheat from around you, and say the like of that, and distribute it Mudd by Mudd to each poor person, and say the like of that.' Dawud said: 'I did the like of that, and it was as if I had been untied from a knot. And more than one person did that, so they benefited by it.'

key_terms.الْمُضْطَرّ: The distressed or needy one, referring to the one who calls out in desperation.
key_terms.بُرّ: Wheat, specifically the grain used for this ritual.
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods, approximately 3 liters.
key_terms.عِقَال: A rope or cord used to tie a camel's legs, used here metaphorically for the feeling of being bound by illness.
key_terms.مُدّ: A smaller unit of volume measurement, one quarter of a Sa'a.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and charitable act for healing illness according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia tradition of combining spiritual supplication with physical remedies, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribed a specific ritual involving wheat and charity to cure Dawud ibn Zurbiyy. The practice highlights the concept of *shifa* (healing) through divine name invocation and the merit of distributing sustenance, reflecting the holistic approach to health in Imami medicine. The widespread adoption of this method underscores its perceived efficacy and the continuity of prophetic healing traditions within the Ahl al-Bayt.
